page.layout: One printed page (361), one text column with marginal notes in the right margin. No running head. Signature "Aaa 2" and catchword "Avicen-" at the foot.

main_text.p: Jacobus AlFirauzabadius] leg. Mohammed Jacobi filius, Kamusi author sc. محمد بن يعقوب بن محمد الشيرازي الفيروزبادي Mohammed Ebn Jaacub Eb Mohammed AlShirazi AlPhiruzabadi, seu Shirazita Firuzabadensis. Natus est anno Hejrae 729, loco dicto كارزين Carazin denatus an.{*} 817.+ Mezh.816. Magnae eruditionis vir, & magno eo nomine apud reges & principes in honore, praecipuè apud Ismaelem Abbasi filium Tamanensem, cui القاموس AlKamus, seu Oceanum linguae Arabicae dedicavit, nec non apud Bajazidum (seu Bajazetem) Tilderim Chan. A Timurlenco (seu Tamerlano) dono accepisse fertur خمسة الاف دينار quinquies mille aureos.AlIannab. Kadi Shohbah.
Safioddinus] sc. صفي الدين عبد المؤمن بن عبد الحق Safioddin AbdolMumen, Ebn Abdilhakki. libri à nobis citati titulus مراصد الاطلاع على اسما الامكنة والبقاع Dictionarium quoddam Geographicum.

R. Saadias] cujus nomen aliàs סעדיה aliàs סעדיא scriptum reperies.p. 34. Hic omnes veteris testamenti libros in linguam Arabicam transtulit, cujus operis pars prima (scil. Pentateuchus) dudum excusa est Constantinopoli, charactere Hebraico, una cum textu Hebr. & versionibus, Chaldaea Onkeli & Persica Jacobi Tusensis, qui vulgo Tawosius dicitur, nuperrimè verò Parisiis Arabico, in splendido isto Bibliorum πολυγλώττων opere.
Iudaeus qui libros Regum in linguam Arabicam vertit.] Anonymus. Alium à Saadia esse stilus indicat.

page.notes: Printed Arabic and Greek and Hebrew transcribed from the scan; the Arabic lines are approximate and should be checked. Doubtful: "AlFirauzabadius" (the z form is unclear); "Abdilhakki" (may read Abdilbakki); Hebrew "סעדיה aliàs סעדיא" (letters unclear, possibly סעריה / סעריא); "Tawosius"; "Tusensis". The asterisk in the text is printed "*" and the margin note bears "+", so the mark may be a mismatch in the original. The note "AlIannab." stands beside the Timurlenco line, and "p. 34." beside the Saadias entry. The entry "Jacobus" opens the page as a fresh entry, not a continuation.
